paper.title: Whole-Body Mobile Manipulation using Offline Reinforcement Learning on Sub-optimal Controllers

review.question: 2025-07-19 至 2026-07-19 的 loco-manipulation 研究在哪些控制、学习、数据、感知、评测和部署方向取得了可验证进展，其适用边界与未解问题是什么？

relevance.reason: Direct whole-body mobile-manipulation learning study using controller-generated offline data and real hardware evaluation.

sections_read.purpose: Inspect WBC data generation and Q-chunking offline RL.
Verify physical drawer and cupboard outcomes.
Record pose estimation and compliance boundaries.

research_question: Can whole-body controller rollouts replace teleoperation data and support offline-RL mobile manipulation on hardware?
contributions: Controller-generated whole-body datasets and a diffusion Q-chunking offline-RL policy.

method.summary: A WBC state machine generates thousands of trajectories; a diffusion policy is optimized with offline Q-learning and deployed as a unified whole-body policy.
assumptions: Task geometry and object pose estimates are sufficiently accurate.
A hand-designed WBC state machine can generate useful task coverage.

embodiments: mobile manipulator in simulation and hardware
study_context.sample_or_scale: Two tasks, 3,000 generated trajectories per task, and 25 real trials per method/task.

evaluation.design: The proposed offline-RL policy is compared with WBC-only and behavior-cloning baselines in simulation and real deployment.

findings.finding: Offline RL improved real cupboard opening over both the generator and behavior cloning, but perception accuracy remained consequential.
findings.scope: Two articulated-object tasks on one physical platform.

author_stated.limitation: Performance remains sensitive to object-pose accuracy and hardware compliance.

reader_inferred.boundary: The approach avoids teleoperation but still embeds task engineering through the WBC generator.
reader_inferred.basis: A task-specific state machine supplies the offline dataset.

transfer_boundary: Best suited to tasks where controller-based data generation and stable pose tracking are available.

design_strengths: Directly compares the learned policy with its data generator.
Reports 25 physical trials per task and method.
design_risks: Marker-based tracking can overstate open-world perception readiness.
critical_appraisal.baseline_fairness: All methods use the same task setup; the learned methods use the controller-generated data.
critical_appraisal.metric_validity: Task and substage success expose where failures occur.
critical_appraisal.reproducibility: Data-generation and training pipelines are described.

evidence_cards.claim: On real cupboard opening, WHOLE-MoMa succeeded in 17/25 trials (68%), versus 4/25 for its WBC generator and 8/25 for behavior cloning.
evidence_cards.relation: Supports offline RL as a way to improve beyond controller-generated whole-body data.
evidence_cards.summary: The real-world table separates full success across the three methods.
evidence_cards.source_context: WHOLE-MoMa achieves 17/25 (68%), demonstrating substantial sim-to-real transfer, with the highest grasping success (22/25) and articulation success (17/22 given grasping).

quantitative.comparator: WHOLE-MoMa versus WBC and behavior cloning

verification.rationale: The result sentence reports all three counts and percentages for the cupboard task.
